claims.text: What the image looks like Anterior mediastinal mass → '4 T's': Thymoma, Teratoma, Thyroid, Terrible lymphoma
claims.quote: Anterior mediastinal mass '4 T's': Thymoma, Teratoma, Thyroid, Terrible lymphoma

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) CT with IV contrast is the most valuable imaging technique; it separates normal variants and benign fat- and fluid-filled cysts from other processes
claims.quote: CT with IV contrast is the most valuable imaging technique. With thoracic CT, normal variants and benign tumors, such as fat- and fluid-filled cysts, can be distinguished from other processes.

claims.text: MRI is done if the structure is cystic, and may show whether the mass is compressing or invading adjacent structures
claims.quote: An MRI is performed if the structure is cystic. MRI may be useful in determining whether the mass is compressing or invading adjacent structures.

claims.text: Often found incidentally on a chest radiograph or other imaging done for chest symptoms
claims.quote: Mediastinal masses are most often incidentally discovered on chest radiograph or other imaging tests during an examination for chest symptoms.

claims.text: Causes Adults, anterior (prevascular) mediastinum: thymomas, benign cysts and lymphomas (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin)
claims.quote: Anterior (prevascular) mediastinum: Thymomas, benign cysts, and lymphomas (both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin)

claims.text: Children, anterior (prevascular): ectopic thyroid, lymphoma, sarcoma, teratoma, thymic lesions
claims.quote: Anterior (prevascular) | Ectopic thyroid Lymphoma Sarcoma Teratoma Thymic lesions
claims.locator: Some Causes of Mediastinal Masses in Children table

claims.text: Symptoms Many are asymptomatic; the most common symptoms are chest pain and weight loss; lymphomas may present with fever and weight loss
claims.quote: Many mediastinal masses are asymptomatic. In general, malignant lesions and masses in children are much more likely to cause symptoms. The most common symptoms are chest pain and weight loss. Lymphomas may manifest with fever and weight loss.

claims.text: Large anterior masses may cause dyspnea when lying supine
claims.quote: Large anterior mediastinal masses may cause dyspnea when patients are lying supine.

claims.text: Children are more likely to have tracheobronchial compression and stridor or recurrent bronchitis or pneumonia
claims.quote: In children, mediastinal masses are more likely to cause tracheobronchial compression and stridor or symptoms of recurrent bronchitis or pneumonia.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: tissue diagnosis
Fine-needle aspiration usually suffices for carcinoma, but a cutting-needle biopsy is needed whenever lymphoma, thymoma or a neural mass is suspected; measure TSH if ectopic thyroid is considered
claims.quote: Fine-needle aspiration techniques usually suffice for carcinomatous lesions, but a cutting-needle biopsy should be performed to provide sufficient tissue for diagnostic analysis whenever lymphoma, thymoma, or a neural mass is suspected. If ectopic thyroid tissue is considered a cause, thyroid-stimulating hormone is measured.

claims.text: Treatment depends on the cause: some benign lesions (eg, pericardial cysts) can be observed; most malignant tumors are removed surgically, but lymphomas are best treated with chemotherapy
claims.quote: Treatment depends on etiology. Some benign lesions, such as pericardial cysts, can be observed. Most malignant tumors should be removed surgically, but some, such as lymphomas, are best treated with chemotherapy.

claims.text: Airway caution: airway compression and hemodynamics can worsen when supine, especially with sedation; biopsy with minimal sedation in an upright or semi-upright position
claims.quote: Because both airway compression and hemodynamic status can worsen when supine, especially with sedation, traditional anesthetic and airway management practices may be dangerous (1). Patients may be transported to definitive care awake and upright. Procedures such as biopsy are performed with minimal sedation while the patient is in an upright or semi-upright position.
